purpose: The one letter this map quotes whose original is digitised outside the Ransom Center.
rights_note: The Library states 'No known restrictions on use or reproduction' for this item and marks it not access-restricted, recorded here as NKC.
notes: Per-page `file` is relative to `../../manuscripts/<key>/`, the private tree that holds the images. The path is metadata; the images are what stays unpublished.
Wilde's five sides read 8, 9, 12, 13, 10 in scan order - the leaves were photographed out of sequence.
Images 6 and 7 are not Wilde: they are Swinburne's letter to him of 2 February 1882, which the quoted letter copies out at length and which was folded in with it.
www.loc.gov refuses a non-browser request, but the image service at tile.loc.gov does not.

items.title: Oscar Wilde to Walt Whitman, [postmark 1 March 1882], with an enclosed letter from A. C. Swinburne to Wilde

pages.caption: archival folder slip: Feinberg-Whitman General Correspondence, Wilde, Oscar, 1882
envelope, addressed 'To Walt Whitman, Camden city, Philadelphia', stamped
dealer's catalogue description: '1882 March 1 Oscar Wilde to Walt Whitman; from New York. A.L.S. (5p.)'
Enclosure: A. C. Swinburne to Wilde, The Pines, Putney Hill, 2 February 1882 - the letter Wilde copies out
Wilde's letter, side 1 of 5: '1267 Broadway, New York. My Dear Dear Walt - Swinburne has just written to me'
Wilde's letter, side 2 of 5: 'in my name, that I have by no manner of means relaxed my admiration'
Wilde's letter, side 5 of 5: 'Essay on Poetry' to the signature - 'With warm affection, and honorable admiration, Oscar Wilde'
Wilde's letter, side 3 of 5: 'most enviable distinction that he never speaks so well'
Wilde's letter, side 4 of 5: 'prepared to bestow on another' to 'a copy of your'
